ratings_why.fun: Lighting a loaded line and watching it go off is a great recruit-phase feeling, and spend versus hold is a real choice; the early turns and Tier 3 are thin on stats.
ratings_why.distinct: A threshold counter that spills along the zigzag, carried by any tribe and aimable at the enemy, plays unlike today's tribes, though Hedgerow already grows along touching runs.

verdict_why: The Thirty-Two of Altenburg loops on itself with two copies, and the early game needs a little more spark; the core is good.

points.text: Two Thirty-Twos each have the other's Blurt text, which includes their own, so the text recurses forever. Make it 'the printed Blurt text of each other unit'.
Turns 1 to 3 rarely reach 3 Gossip, so the tribe is a pile of vanilla bodies until Tier 3. Start the Taster and Huddler with 1 Gossip, as the design's own risks suggest.

Almost every payoff is a flat +1/+1 a Blurt, so the late game grows only with chain count. One share-based payoff (for example, the Bean-Counter giving a share of its stats) would give the curve a top end without the golden stack.
Ilse, the Speaker and the Squeaker give no stats themselves, so Tier 3 can leave you weak in fights. A small Blurt text on Ilse would help the mid-game.
With the Bellringer or Echo it's unclear whether 'three times a turn' counts Blurts or text uses. Say which.

standouts.why: The Bean-Counter turns line order into the puzzle: put it last and a long chain pays it the most.
The Bad Omen turns the tribe's own mechanic on the enemy, and gaps in the enemy board are clear counterplay.
Speaker Brotkrume as a 1-Gossip hub that reaches every slot next to it reshapes the wire in a way you can see.

weakest.why: Taster Wendelin is a 1/3 that Blurts about once a turn for +1/+1, too slow to matter early.
Floorboard Squeaker only works in the front row and gives no stats; it's filler outside the hold build.
Cold-Shed Tangle's 1/1 Strays are low value at Tier 4 unless you're feeding Oozes.

flags.note: Two copies give each other's Blurt text recursively, with no end.
The Rat King makes a 5+ Blurt chain every Start of Turn, so with the King the Wall-Runner is a free Discover every turn.
Fed by Fuse Attack buffs, one Omen hit can chain through a gapless enemy board and hit every unit for half its Attack.
A board held at two pips makes up to seven attacks at Start of Combat before the enemy acts.
Whether the three-a-turn cap counts Blurts or extra text uses from the Bellringer or Echo.
